body:
**Ruling on the open question: option A. Ship as-is — the fixture asserts 5 of 6 and pins the sixth as blind BY NAME.**

The dispatch asked for a fixture "asserting the gate now reports **them**" — all six. This PR reports five. I am confirming that as correct and recording why, because the deviation is from my instruction and the dev was right to flag it rather than quietly meet the letter of it.

### Why A and not B

The card's item 1 is explicit: *"Make the parser see the bare `:NNN` continuation form, **or** narrow the charter … ⛔ Not both silently — pick one and say which."* This PR picked the parser and said so. Widening the proximity window is a **second, independent change to a false-positive guard**, and the card reserved that guard by name in its own ⛔ Not-measured list: *"whether the 2-line proximity window is deliberate (it may be guarding against false positives, in which case the fix is charter-side, not parser-side)."*

⭐ **The measurement that settles it, and it is the strongest reading in this PR:** with the trigger absent and the window widened to **999999**, the docblock still reads **0 of 6**. ⇒ the window was measurably **not the cause** of the blindness, so leaving it untouched is not an omission — it is the correct scope. A change that had moved the window would have confounded the two.

### Why the residual is not a hole

The card's actual complaint is not "the gate misses one address." It is that *"a report-only gate that cannot parse the form it claims to watch reports a clean sheet"* — the failure is **self-concealing**. Pinning the sixth address as blind **by name**, in the test, converts that silence into a declaration. ⇒ the defect class is closed even though one address stays out of scope, and ⛔ it can no longer be mistaken for coverage, which was the whole finding.

The control does what the card demanded: **0 → 5**, with an ablation on the committed code returning it to 0 (`AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 601, 625, 640, 747, 865 ]`, restored byte-identical). Green was replaced by red.

### B is not dropped, it is measured and routed

Widening to a window of 5 costs **+14 rows** tree-wide — 11 real citations against 1 port, 1 cron minute and 1 Chinese enumeration. That is a defensible ratio and a genuine decision, so it goes on its own card rather than into this PR. ⛔ It is not a condition on landing this one.

### Also on the record

- ⭐ Enforcement stays **report-only** and the gate reports 0 new citations on this PR's own diff. That was the way this PR could have gone badly wrong — a parser that starts seeing a form while the gate is enforcing reddens every open PR — and it did not.
- The backlog was measured **before** the parser moved (1201 → 1271, false 532 → 561), with a faithfulness control showing the candidate switched off reproduces the shipped census row-for-row. That ordering was the card's item 3 and it was honoured.
- ~8 of the 74 newly visible rows are ports and JSON literals rather than citations. Naming them in the PR body instead of hand-tuning them away is the right call: every structural filter measured to remove them also removed **real** citations.

⛔ Nothing further is owed from the dev on this PR. Landing waits only on terminal CI.

## Landing provenance — PR #9082 (card objectui#9026)

Head: **`5b71f126bbe0954808327733d59a636041f1edeb`**. Gate checkout: fresh `objectstack` clone `os-fresh2`, `origin/main` = `ef180302f55955baf9994a91d0793bbd3926b068`.

### ① contract review — NOT OWED

`Clause-②: no`, and both carriers are absent and agreeing (card objectui#9026 carries no `needs:contract-review`; this PR's labels are `tests` only). ⛔ No PASS record is cited because none exists and none is owed.

### ② the enqueue gates — including one that FAILED first

| gate | exact command | exit |
|---|---|---|
| carriers + C5 | `PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 9082` | **4 → 0** |
| widening tells | `PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff <PR diff>` | 0, **NOT MEASURED** — see below |
| governed surface | `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr objectstack-ai/objectui#9082` | **0** — 0 of 4 paths hit the register |

⭐ **The carriers gate failed first, at exit 4, and the defect was the seat's — recorded rather than quietly fixed.** Its finding:

> the `Clause-②` declaration is MISPLACED: the fixed spelling appears on the thread … but NOT in the card's claim comment, which is the carrier the enqueue gate's content limb reads.

`check-clause2-carriers.mjs:751-752` defines a claim comment as one whose body carries **a LINE BEGINNING `Claim:`**. I had been opening claims with `**Claim:**`, so the line begins `**` and **no comment on the card was a claim comment at all** by the predicate. Measured across tonight's claims: objectui#8735 and objectui#8784 used the bare spelling and passed `--pair` at exit 0; objectui#9026, objectui#9034, objectui#8832, objectui#8924 and objectui#8811 used `**Claim:**` and were illegible. On objectui#9034 I had also bolded the value — `Clause-②: **yes**` — defeating even a loose match.

⇒ Four live cards were repaired with format-only claim comments (same session, same branch, same declaration; ⛔ not re-claims), each verified against the gate's own predicate before re-running. The re-run returns **exit 0**: *"the clause-② declaration is readable in the fixed spelling and both carriers agree."*

⛔ **Markdown emphasis on a field a machine reads is not formatting, it is corruption** — and the failure was self-concealing in the same shape this very card is about: the gate reported not "this is wrong" but "there is nothing here to read".

### ⚠️ What the widening-tells gate does NOT say here

Exit 0, and ⛔ **it is not a clean reading.** The tool says so itself, and I am quoting it rather than paraphrasing:

> ⛔ NOTHING on this diff was examined for widening tells, so this exit 0 is evidence about no surface at all.

All **4 of 4** paths are NOT MEASURED — no declared surface covers `.changeset/9026-bare-colon-continuation-scope.md`, `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs`, or either file under `scripts/__tests__/`.

⚠️ My firing control **fired** (T1 `:12`, T2 `:15`, exit 4) but on `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts` — **a path this PR does not touch**. ⇒ it establishes the tool works; it does ⛔ **not** establish that a tell could have fired on this PR's paths, because no tell can fire there at all.

⇒ The support for "this diff widens nothing" is therefore the **governed-surface predicate** (0 of 4 paths, derived from `GOVERNED_SURFACES` on the final file list) and the file list itself — ⛔ not the tells.

### ③ every check, not a required subset

34 check-runs on `5b71f126…`: **31 `success` + 3 `skipped`, 0 non-green**, all `completed`. Reported `total_count` 34 == returned array length 34, so nothing hid behind pagination. ⚠️ At 00:09Z this same head had **9 checks still `in_progress`** — that state was read as not-terminal and landing waited, because ⛔ an `in_progress` check is not a green one.

`mergeable_state` moved `behind` → `clean`. ⛔ `behind` was never treated as a blocker: the merge queue rebuilds each PR on current `main` itself, and hand-merging the base would move the head.

### charter provenance, with its own controls

The seven governing files are byte-identical between the clone's `ad715aca57…` and current `main` `ef180302f5…`. Controls: the same two commits diff to **36 files / +3466 / -147** with no path filter, and each of the seven paths resolves to a real blob (not `MISSING`) at both revs. ⛔ No "no output above = clean" echo is written for that empty path-scoped diff.

### carriers

Neither carrier holds `needs:contract-review`, so there is nothing to strip. Landing by **squash** through the merge queue.
